channel.title: There Is No First SCP Curse!
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "There Is No First SCP Curse!" - What does a successful first SCP look like? Much like any other SCP! Let's talk about that.

item.title: Re: There Is No First SCP Curse!
item.content:encoded:
If an author has a good idea, it's not difficult to get greenlit, especially if an experienced reviewer writes a positive response.

The large majority of concepts generated by brand new authors tend to be scrapped or postponed as they'd either need a lot of edits to be workable or would take a lot of extra effort to draft well, hence the low rate of greenlights observed.

item.title: Re: There Is No First SCP Curse!
item.content:encoded:
SCP-4612 is the first thing I wrote for the wiki, and so far its my most popular. I went through critique in the forums and on discord and spent probably 3 weeks polishing it up, then made the leap and posted. I went through greenlighting and draft critique, and though the process can be intimidating, I am glad i did so.

Secret really is to take critique with an open mind, and it can only improve your article. And there are lots of experienced authors who are willing to help.

And like Calibri said above, don't worry if your original idea doesn't work… its actually fairly likely, even if you have experience writing (i've written for the past 10 years, for example) because something might work elsewhere in fiction but not so much for the wiki

Best advice anyone gave me (weizhong) is that this is flash fiction: look at each part of your draft and if its not there for a specific purpose, consider cutting it. Be as economical as you can be.

item.title: Re: There Is No First SCP Curse!
item.content:encoded:
SCP-4645 is my first article ever, my first attempt at an article ever, and remains my highest-rated article at over +200 now. I can tell you with complete honestly that the only reason I succeeded with my first article was by getting greenlights in the ideas forum, then writing a draft and getting crit on that, and then posting after the draft had gone through enough crit. I cannot stress this enough: get greenlights on your idea before you write a draft! Yes, you are going to start out with ideas that don't work out well. I had two ideas on the forums that flopped before I finally came up with my mega cool blackmailing computer idea. The entire process took me over a month, from first trying to come up with ideas to posting my completed work to the forums, and I can say with 100% certainty that the results were worth every second of that time.

I see plenty of folks say that the ideas forum is "too restrictive" or "just isn't for them". I can tell you right now that I would not have written a successful article had I not gone through that process and taken the time to make an idea that works. You will not regret going through the greenlight process, it will seriously help you. It is a system which benefits everyone involved. Patience is key. It could take months for you to get solid footing, but I guarantee you'll learn from the experience, and your time will not be wasted. But if you rush an article, I can pretty much guarantee it will fail, and you'll have wasted all that time working on it anyway.

I know all of this is basically just stuff that's covered in the guides, but I feel like it needs to be said here as well, because it really was the main reason I succeeded.

TL;DR: Get greenlights on an idea, then write a draft, then get crit on the draft, then post the draft, all in that exact order. Don't become too attached to your ideas, because there's a good chance they won't work. And be patient. Good work is never rushed.

item.title: Re: There Is No First SCP Curse!
item.content:encoded:
This thread is ancient but I felt like putting my two cents in for the hell of it.

I believe the majority of those who say there is a "First SCP Curse", believe this because they created one without, as implied before, learning the basics of how to actually write out an SCP article or tale before doing so, and waiting until after it's written to fully take the time to research The Foundation's Forums. One of which can unironically be found under How To Write An SCP. (Super helpful by the by).

+ show block
– hide block

Moral is, we have wheelbarrows of forums and articles telling you exactly what you need to know and when. Just give 'em a look and you'll be happy you did. And hell, even if you miss a couple things here and there, you got staff in every corner for that kind of thing; especially when putting your ideas and drafts into their respected forums. Nonetheless, even if you do want to jump right in to writing an article, take a moment to skim what you have and metaphorically sit on your idea.
Thank yourself later.

item.title: Re: There Is No First SCP Curse!
item.content:encoded:
SCP-4098 is my first SCP and it has kept itself alive for over 2 weeks.

Even with my habit of literally writing an article without stopping my hands at all feigning me off, I still managed it.

Everyone has doubts about their first SCP. Just don't give up, anything can be an SCP, anything at all (as long as it breaks the laws of nature, physics, etc.), all that is needed is to try and reach into the deeper recesses of your imagination to be able to make a great skip.

item.title: Re: There Is No First SCP Curse!
item.content:encoded:
I'll say this: contests are a great way for new authors to get noticed. Writing into the contest theme can also help with solidifying your writing. Also, I did my homework. Read ALL the guides. They help.

My first SCP went up on the second day of the 4000 Contest, and was in the first twenty, so it got early attention. (It's worth noting that with the exception of the excellent Someone to Watch Over Us, the bulk of the top ten went up in the first few days). It has a strong concept, though the execution took quite a bit of time before it was in its final state (early versions were a bit unfocussed). But, the free attention from the contest meant that it kept on climbing, and once it had momentum it kept going. It finished up eighth overall in the contest at +188, and I was able to get some prime real estate for it upon resolution, which has further helped.

SCP-4001, Alexandria Eternal is currently past +300 +350 and still climbing.

Alas, it feels like I'm under the other first SCP curse. Nothing else I've written is remotely close to how successful Alexandria is. It has more points than everything else I've written put together, and is probably going to stay like that for a long time.

item.title: Re: There Is No First SCP Curse!
item.content:encoded:
Probably because you posted it without asking feedback first.

We would like to remind you that as mentioned in the required reading, members are expected to create a Sandbox Page for their draft before posting it on the main site. After doing this, we highly encourage making a thread for your SCP idea and ask for feedback in the feedback forum. Other users and members of the Forum Critique Team will gladly help you out.

Writing standards in terms of formatting and narrative are high on the SCP wiki. We are more than willing to help you get off the ground, but you have to help yourself as well.

If you have any questions about this, don't hesitate to PM me or another member of staff.

item.title: Re: There Is No First SCP Curse!
item.content:encoded: Another reason why not many first SCP’s make it is because you guys hurry too much on typing and posting your article. You end up missing vital errors in them, and it would have most likely succeeded if it had been critiqued. A reason why most deleted articles don’t make it is because they weren’t posted in the critique forums first, because they thought “Oh I don’t need critiques, it’s good enough to me as it is”. A lot of these deleted articles have really good ideas, but they are executed poorly, which is really sad. Don’t rush your articles, take your time editing and receiving feedback until you think that your article could literally not get any better.

item.title: Re: There Is No First SCP Curse!
item.content:encoded:
Failure is reality, a sad naturalistic consequence.

No one who has ever existed has been successful at every single thing they've done. That said, no one who has ever existed has been a complete failure at every single thing they've done.

Failure happens. So does success. First and foremost though, writing for the site should be a hobby. If you're getting upset while writing here, that's a sign that maybe it's a good idea to take a breather and stop forcing yourself to do something that you dislike in your spare time.

Also, for the record:

Could I make a successful SCP in hindsight? If I started over? Flirted with users in chat perhaps to earn brownie points?

I don't recommend the flirting. Not only does it run the risk of coming off as creepy, it's kind of underhanded to assume that people will automatically upvote things solely based on whether they like the author or not (which is against the rules, as it is).

item.title: Re: There Is No First SCP Curse!
item.content:encoded:
There's no such thing as curses.

There are however… hurdles, obstacles, obstructions, to overcome. It doesn't matter how much of a good writer you are. Makes no difference if you've written science-fiction novels on other sites. If you don't understand THIS site, i.e. you comprehend the backstory, the lore, the community's expectations (then and now), the requirements for writing an SCP or developing a tale. If you don't take these into consideration and act accordingly: Your article will fail. Mine hit the ground fairly hard, and I took it personally. Eventually I managed to get one that stuck, somewhat, and what remains is in the lowest rated pages of all time. Congrats?

Could I make a successful SCP in hindsight? If I started over? Flirted with users in chat perhaps to earn brownie points? Probably not. Again, writing and reading SCPs in general is just not universal/suitable for all audiences. Just as some may succeed in creating them, many will fail, like developing games - its hard - and you can go wrong. Failure is reality, a sad naturalistic consequence.

This is probably not the place to ask this, it's not on topic. This thread is about debunking the perception that first SCPs always fail. You probably should have just started a thread in Questions Desk.

Anyway, no. That notation is for quantities where precision is required and small mistakes are dangerous, like drug dosing. It makes little sense for things like room dimensions (nobody is going to cause a problem if they accidentally say that a distance is 3.5 m instead of 3.6) and makes it difficult to read.

item.title: my experience
item.content:encoded:
Every writer expects their first SCP to be the exception and I was no different. I thought, "oh, this is such a good idea, how could this fail?" and yet, watching it get downvoted within an hour of posting and down 15 within 15 hours, I came to a realization; I had done close to everything wrong.

My first SCP (and you were unlikely to have seen it prior to deletion) was SCP 3664. The basic idea was that it was the heart of, "mankind's mother," that had been severed by her miscarried young and turned into a massive biological organism with spreading nerve fibers and constantly birthing blood colored entities that liquified to prevent losses. The problem? I had no experience with proper expungement or good SCP layout. It was a Keter SCP, and that was probably my first mistake; Keters are often the hardest to write about because they require a substantially better understanding of SCP standards that commonly seen. but more than that was just the overall layout and terrible use of expungement. if you can find it in the deleted section, there was a very helpful comment from a site administrator explaining everything that went wrong, and you can look there for yourself.
I was the faun, taking his first steps on shaky legs, only to find his first step too ambitious and falling flat.
So my plan going forward? try again with less ambitious goals. something simpler, something that can ease me into the water until I feel that I have a good enough understanding of the proper method so that I can go back and edit my original work into something not only I feel proud of, but everyone can read and enjoy.
So the first SCP curse? It doesn't exist. But that doesn't mean no one feels it. Hell, it's actually given me a decent idea for a joke SCP that I'm near positive has been done before.
Sincerely,
Abbhorase.
